newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam car market set for acceleration.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam car market set for acceleration.

text.p: Demand for cars in Vietnam, a country where the most popular form of transport is still the bicycle, is set to more than double by 2000, the vice-minister for industry said in an interview published on Sunday.
Nguyen Xuan Chuan told the weekly Vietnam Investment Review that the market would grow from 35,000 units in 1995 to over 80,000 by the turn of the century and then more than 120,000 by 2005.
"Quantitively, this is not many cars to have to sell," Chuan said, defending the government's recent decision to license the country's 13th joint-venture for car production.
State media reports said last week that Nissan Motors Corp and Marubeni Trading Corp would soon receive a licence to begin work on what would be the 14th automobile plant in Vietnam.

Chuan said the total design capacities of the 13 licensed plants stood at 180,000 cars per year. But the manufacturers were not planning to reach that level for 10 to 15 years, by which time demand would be higher than 180,000 a year.
"At the moment, many car assemblers contend that the number of car joint ventures is too large, so they have to consider their investment plans," Chuan said.
"If any partner thinks that they could compete in Vietnam and accept all the fundamental conditions of the government, there is no reason not to grant licenses to them."
Vietnam's economy has been one of the fastest-growing in the world since capitalist-style reforms to the command economy began to bite in the ealy 1990s.

Although rapid economic growth has brought a jump in incomes and livings standards, only a tiny proportion of Vietnam's 75 million people own a car. According to 1995 figures, just 3.5 percent of households owned a car in Ho Chi Minh City, the country's economic hub.
